instruction: Write a JavaScript function readFile(path, callback) in Node.js style that invokes callback(err, data), calling callback with an Error when the path is empty.
Write a JavaScript mapWith(arr, fn) higher-order function that applies fn to every element and returns a new array, without using Array.prototype.map.
Write a JavaScript function applyTwice(fn, value) that calls fn on the result of the first call.
Write a JavaScript compose(f, g) that returns a function applying g first then f: compose(f, g)(x) === f(g(x)).
Write a JavaScript once wrapper for a callback-style function so the underlying callback only ever fires once.
Write a JavaScript function delayCallback(fn, ms, ...args) that invokes fn with args after ms milliseconds via setTimeout.
Write a JavaScript forEachWith(arr, fn) that mimics Array.prototype.forEach including the index and array arguments and ignores the return value.
Write a JavaScript someWith(arr, predicate) that returns true as soon as the predicate matches one element, without using Array.prototype.some.
Write a JavaScript curry2(fn) that curries a two-argument function: curry2(fn)(a)(b) === fn(a, b).
Write a JavaScript partial(fn, ...preset) helper that pre-fills leading arguments and returns a function taking the rest.
Write a JavaScript function callbackToPromise(fn) that wraps a Node-style callback function (err, result) into one returning a Promise.
Write a JavaScript adder(base) function returning a function that adds its argument to the captured base each call.
Write a JavaScript walkTree(node, visit) recursive callback that calls visit on every node of a nested {value, children} tree in depth-first order.
Write a JavaScript class Greeter with methods that use bind so the callbacks keep the correct this when passed around.
Write a JavaScript sortWith(arr, compareFn) that sorts using a comparator callback, and use it to sort numbers descending.
Write a JavaScript registerHandler(eventName, handler) and emit(eventName, payload) pair that dispatches to registered callbacks.
Write a JavaScript retry(times, fn, callback) that calls fn up to times times, passing the final error or result to callback.
Write a JavaScript memoizeWith(fn, keyFn) that caches by a custom key derived from the arguments via keyFn.
Write a JavaScript safeCall(fn, args, onError) that invokes fn, catching synchronous exceptions and routing them to onError.
Write a JavaScript pipeline(...fns) that chains unary functions left-to-right: pipeline(f, g, h)(x) === h(g(f(x))).
